In Arm E, both the driver and the instrument behave as designed: the behavior comes from **Arm E's design** (`CONSENT_IN_CODE = False`), which trusts the reader model's `"yes"` on consent questions whenever code cannot deterministically parse confirmation.

### Root Cause
1. In [dcitl_f.py](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_f.py#L17-L39), `DcitlE` sets `CONSENT_IN_CODE = False` (unlike `DcitlF`, which sets `CONSENT_IN_CODE = True`).
2. During booking ([Driver.book](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L482-L493)) and rescheduling ([Driver.reschedule](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L601-L610)), when [explicit_confirm](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L156-L167) returns `None` (e.g., a multi-word rejection like `"No, I can't do that one. Here's what I can do..."` exceeding the 4-word threshold, or an ambiguous/hedged reply), the driver delegates to [Driver.consent](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L264-L271).
3. Under Arm E (`self.consent_in_code == False`), a `"yes"` from the reader model (such as [AlwaysYes.ask](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_f.py#L64-L69)) causes `Driver.consent` to return `True`, immediately committing `commit_booking()` or `do_move()`. Under Arm F (`self.consent_in_code == True`), `Driver.consent` treats a model `"yes"` as `None` (unclear), re-asks, and hands off to staff after two unclear replies.

hypotheses.cause: By design, Arm E (`DcitlE`) sets `consent_in_code=False`, so whenever `explicit_confirm` returns `None` on a booking or reschedule reply, `Driver.consent` accepts a reader model's `"yes"` (including `AlwaysYes`) as consent and commits the write. Arm F (`DcitlF`) sets `consent_in_code=True`, so `Driver.consent` ignores a model `"yes"` and re-asks or hands off instead.
